title: Why inference is the new bottleneck
intro: Good open models are everywhere now. Running them cheaply is the hard part.

steps.title: Training happens once, inference forever
steps.body:
Most AI cost is **inference, not training**. Training is a one-off; inference bills you *every single time a user sends a message*. And since thousands of competitive open models now sit on Hugging Face (Llama, Qwen, Mistral, DeepSeek, gpt-oss…), the question has flipped from *"can I get a good model?"* to *"can I run it efficiently?"*

Self-hosting pays four ways: **cost** (match model size to task), **security** (data never leaves), **control** (no rate limits or third-party downtime), **customization** (fine-tune).

steps.title: Fast enough AND accurate enough
steps.body: A deployment needs **SLOs** — measurable targets on both axes. Accuracy must clear the usability bar for *your* use case (check the model card). Performance is measured in four numbers:

points.label: TTFT
points.note: Time to first token — how long the user waits before anything appears. Chatbot SLO: ≤200 ms at p99.

points.label: ITL
points.note: Inter-token latency — the gap between streamed tokens. Governs how smooth the answer feels.

points.label: E2E
points.note: Full request latency, first to last token. What a non-streaming client experiences.

points.label: Throughput
points.note: Output tokens/sec across ALL requests — whether you survive production scale.

steps.title: The tradeoff triangle
steps.body: **Accuracy ↔ Performance ↔ Cost: pick two.** Faster answers need more compute; bigger models cost more; aggressive optimization can dent accuracy. Good tooling doesn't repeal the triangle — it pushes the frontier outward.

viz.caption: A naive full-precision deployment: accurate, but slow and expensive. The rest of this pack moves the other two corners.

steps.title: Feel the 10×
steps.body: Naive serving (full precision, one request at a time) costs **$100Ks–$millions per month**. vLLM's batching alone is ~10× cheaper; a quantized model cuts it again. This machine is the physics of that claim — every decode step streams the whole weight tensor, so **batch** amortises it and **precision** shrinks it:

viz.title: The token factory
viz.caption: Start at batch 1 (the naive deployment). Raise the batch, then drop the precision — that's the 10×.

recap: Inference dominates cost because it recurs per message. Define SLOs on **both** axes — accuracy (model card) and performance (TTFT / ITL / e2e latency / throughput, at percentiles) — then optimize inside the accuracy↔performance↔cost triangle. Batching and quantization are the two big levers.
